The dense stereo mesh is computed from the fused depth cloud and includes meshing interpolation. The conservative alternatives show only small facets with explicit multiview support. Masked historical experiments default to scan-group-screened facets, requiring three candidate capture groups at each used vertex; suspected scan copies cannot supply extra support. The historical calibration remains uncertain.

RESEARCH BASIS

What changed after reading Snavely's work.

Scene Chronology (2014), §4.1 starts with SfM and dense CMVS/PMVS patches, then reasons about time. Neural Scene Chronology (2023), §3.1 assumes mostly static geometry. Its official custom-data pipeline requires COLMAP, dense reconstruction, mesh selection, and transient-object filtering.

GhostMap now reconstructs the historical surface separately, uses 1,600px SuperPoint with 8,192 keypoints and exhaustive historical pairing, and runs OpenMVS depth consistency on CPU. Fusion requires at least three supporting images. Artificial tower seeds and hole closing are disabled. The official OpenMVS binaries run with an isolated project-local runtime.

Automatic historical pipeline

  1. Acquire public Wikimedia Commons photographs and Cornell archival IIIF scans with source and rights records: 26 eligible historical images.
  2. Predict building, foliage, and sky masks with a pinned CLIPSeg model. Filter SuperPoint / LightGlue correspondences: 23,411 → 13,199 matches; no manual masks.
  3. Estimate cameras with COLMAP under explicit focal priors. The masked runs register 16 / 17 images at focal ratios 0.8 / 1.2.
  4. Compute CPU multiview depth, consistency, and three-view fusion at up to 1,600px: 20,555 / 13,702 fused points.
  5. Mesh the actual dense cloud, project calibrated source photographs onto it, and audit geometry provenance. The two historical meshes contain 32,632 / 18,046 faces.

These are partial historical scene hypotheses, not a verified complete Boardman building. The new configuration changes both semantic filtering and stereo resolution; its higher point count is not evidence that masking alone improves accuracy. Cornell archive access does not establish a redistribution license.

Files are not independent cameras

A global homography and warped-image correlation screen flags four pairs in two possible repeated-exposure groups, including differently colored postcard scans. Grouping them reduces the masked runs' 16 / 17 registered files to 13 / 14 candidate exposure groups. Only 11,131 / 4,107 dense vertices retain three-group support. The historical default shows local facets satisfying this stricter screen. Thresholds are exploratory; nonflagged images are not thereby certified independent, and geometry was not re-estimated after grouping. Download pair measurements and support audit ↗

Calibration sensitivity

Unconstrained focal optimization produced physically implausible focal estimates despite small reprojection residuals. Fixed priors of 0.8, 1.2, and 1.8 image widths test how strongly the available scans determine geometry. These priors are hypotheses, not measured camera calibration. In the masked runs, 541 shared tracks still move by a median 11.2% of scene radius after similarity alignment between the 0.8 and 1.2 models. This measures sensitivity, not ground-truth error.
